posts.why: The order of information is the whole lesson of the sell week.

tiktok.hook: This site wants a deposit before it tells you what it does.
tiktok.vo: This site opens with book a call, then pay a deposit, and somewhere after that it explains what they sell. The order is backwards. Price comes after clarity, always, because a customer who understands the offer will ask about the money themselves. A customer who does not understand it will not pay a deposit to find out.
tiktok.cap: Deposit first, explanation later. That is a filter, not a funnel.
tiktok.body: Book a call, pay a deposit, then find out what the business does. The order is backwards: price comes after clarity, always. Someone who understands the offer asks about money themselves.

instagram.cap:
A deposit asks for trust before the site has earned any. Put the offer first and the deposit becomes a decision rather than a gamble.

If step three is the explanation, steps one and two will not happen.

facebook.body:
A site I looked at opens with 'book a call', then 'pay a deposit', and only after that explains what they sell.

The order is backwards. Price comes after clarity, always.

A customer who understands your offer will ask about the money themselves. A customer who does not understand it will not pay a deposit to find out.

Which order is yours in?

posts.topic: Buying a template to avoid a decision
posts.why: Names the real reason people buy and never use.

tiktok.hook: Buying a template to avoid a decision is expensive therapy.
beats: Templates only help if you already chose
tiktok.vo: Buying a template to avoid a decision is expensive therapy. The purchase feels like progress, so you get the relief of having done something without doing the thing, which is choosing. The decision is the product. A template only helps you execute a decision you have already made, and it cannot make it for you.
tiktok.cap: The purchase feels like progress. The decision is the progress.
tiktok.body: Buying a template to avoid a decision is expensive therapy. The purchase feels like progress without the discomfort of choosing, and the choosing is the whole job.

instagram.cap:
This is why so many downloads sit unopened while the business stays exactly the same shape. Nothing was decided, so nothing changed.

A template executes a decision. It cannot make one.

facebook.body:
Buying a template to avoid a decision is expensive therapy.

The purchase feels like progress, so you get the relief of having done something without doing the thing — which is choosing.

The decision is the product. A template only helps you execute a decision you have already made.

What are you avoiding deciding?

posts.topic: What would make you pay for a document
posts.why: Validates the price point with the audience's own logic.

tiktok.hook: I asked what would make someone pay five thousand for a document.
beats: If it saves me a whole day
tiktok.vo: I asked what would make people pay five thousand naira for a document. Nobody mentioned the page count or the design. One man said if it saves me a whole day, five thousand is cheap, because a day is worth more than that. Which is the entire pricing logic for anything you sell as information: how many hours does it give back.
tiktok.cap: "If it saves me a whole day." That is what people are buying.
tiktok.body: Nobody mentioned page count or design. The answer was: if it saves me a whole day, five thousand is cheap. You are selling hours back, not pages.

instagram.cap:
The same logic works when you price your own service. Customers compare the cost to the time or the loss, not to your effort.

Price against the day it saves, not the pages it fills.

facebook.body:
I asked what would make people pay ₦5,000 for a document.

Nobody mentioned page count or design.

One man said: 'If it saves me a whole day, ₦5,000 is cheap.'

That is the entire pricing logic for anything sold as information. You are selling hours back, not pages.

What would make it worth ₦5,000 to you?

posts.topic: A refund on an opened download
posts.why: Explains the policy before anyone asks, which prevents resentment.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked for a refund on an opened download.
beats: So the rule is stated up front
And it is on the page
tiktok.vo: Someone asked for a refund two days after downloading a pack and using three of the files. We said no, kindly, and explained: a digital file cannot be returned, so the refund window closes when the download starts, and that is written on the page before you pay. We offered to answer questions about the files instead, which we did, and it ended fine. The policy is not the unfriendly part. Surprising someone with it is.
tiktok.cap: The policy is not the unfriendly part. Springing it on someone is.
tiktok.body: Digital files cannot be returned, so the window closes when the download starts, and that is written on the page before anyone pays. Withholding it until after is what makes a policy feel like a trap.

instagram.cap:
The difference between a firm policy and a bad experience is entirely about when the buyer learned it.

State the rule before the money. Every time.

facebook.body:

We offered to answer questions about the files instead. We did. It ended fine.

The policy is not the unfriendly part. Springing it on someone is.

Where do you state your terms?
